newsitem.title: CHINA: Cheung Kong sparks debate on Hongkong Land bid.
newsitem.headline: Cheung Kong sparks debate on Hongkong Land bid.

text.p: Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd's purchase of a stake in Hongkong Land Holdings Ltd and Jardine Matheson Holdings Ltd sparked speculation on Tuesday that it may make a bid for the companies.

Jardine Matheson announced on Tuesday that Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd and its Hutchison Whampoa Ltd unit together held a 3.03 percent stake in Jardine Matheson and a 3.06 percent stake in Hongkong Land as of August 1.
While analysts said Cheung Kong's motives were unclear, the acquisition sparked debate about a possible takeover bid.
"The opinion on this is quite split at the moment," said Nam Park, an analyst at ING Barings.
"The positive school of thought is that this could begin to herald a new takeover bid for Hongkong Land," he said.
Cheung Kong, along with several other blue chip companies, made a raid on Hongkong Land in 1987.

Following the October 1987 stock market crash, the raiders sold the shares back to the Jardine group and made a gentlemen's agreement not to attempt another takeover for seven or eight years, analysts said.
"Obviously the time is up," said Park.
Jardine Matheson Holdings managing director Alasdair Morrison would not directly respond to the speculation in an interview with Reuters on Tuesday.
"We just believe that they bought the shares because they recognise good value in the companies," he said.
But Hongkong Land and Jardine Matheson shares jumped sharply in Singapore after the announcement on speculation of a repeat of the 1987 raid on the Jardine group, Singapore brokers said.
Jardine Matheson shares surged 17 percent to a high of US$8.25 before closing on a gain of US$0.80 at US$7.85.
Shares of Hongkong Land jumped US$0.57, or 22 percent, to finish at US$3.12.
"If you look at Cheung Kong, at any sort of takeover bid, I think it is extremely unlikely given the present shareholding structure of Hongkong Land," an analyst at an Asian house said.

The Jardine group holds about 32 percent of Hongkong Land through Jardine Strategic Holdings Ltd, which was set up after the 1987 raid as an investment vehicle to hold the Jardine group's investments in listed companies.
Mark Simpson, head of research at Schroder Securities, said Cheung Kong was probably building up a stake in Jardine Matheson and HongkongLand to have access to Hongkong Land's assets.
"They are trying to greenmail assets out of the Hongkong Land portfolio," he said.
Hongkong Land is the largest landlord in Central, Hong Kong's business district.
"Cheung Kong might be counting on those assets for redevelopment. Obviously that will fit in to their existing focus of redevelopment with Cheung Kong Tower," Simpson said.
Analysts said Cheung Kong would produce about 2.0 million square feet of office space in Central in the coming three or four years.
Buying a stake in Jardine Matheson rather than Jardine Strategic would give the Cheung Kong group more influence over the Jardine group's management, Simpson said.
Park also said he did not expect a takeover bid.
"At this stage, we do not believe that these three percent stakes form the beginnings of a takeover bid for HKL or JMH by Cheung Kong and/or Hutchison," he said.
"Why give your hand away in a takeover bid of HKL (or for that matter JMH) with just a three percent stake," Park said in a report.
